stem: A pancreas transplant recipient becomes hypotensive with poor skin turgor and decreased urine output. Which complication should the coordinator prioritize in the differential?

options.text: Dehydration with risk of pancreas graft thrombosis from inadequate perfusion
Expected benign finding that never threatens graft perfusion
Isolated cosmetic issue unrelated to intravascular volume
Mandated indication for immediate graft pancreatectomy in every case

explanation.rationale_correct: The pancreas graft is a low blood-flow organ with higher thrombosis potential; dehydration signs such as poor skin turgor and decreased urine output require prompt reporting because adequate intravascular volume is needed for graft perfusion.

rationale_incorrect.B: Dehydration can compromise pancreas graft perfusion and is not a benign expected finding.
rationale_incorrect.C: Poor skin turgor and oliguria reflect volume depletion with graft risk rather than cosmetic concerns.
rationale_incorrect.D: Volume resuscitation and team evaluation are required; immediate graft removal is not mandated for every dehydration episode.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 15, Pancreas Transplantation → postoperative monitoring → graft thrombosis risk
primary_anchor.quote_hint: low blood flow organ … higher potential for graft thrombosis … maintaining an appropriate intravascular volume

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 15 → postoperative monitoring (low-flow pancreas graft thrombosis risk; dehydration signs require prompt reporting); PDF p. 838 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

stem: Six weeks after heart-lung transplantation, a recipient develops fever and graft dysfunction. Which diagnostic step aligns with standard references when infection may mimic rejection?

options.text: Endomyocardial biopsy to distinguish toxoplasmosis from rejection
No biopsy because infection and rejection are always clinically identical without workup
Permanent discontinuation of all immunosuppression without evaluation
Urinary amylase measurement as the sole diagnostic test for heart-lung recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Toxoplasmosis can mimic rejection in heart transplant recipients; endomyocardial biopsy is required for definitive diagnosis when clinical presentation is ambiguous.

rationale_incorrect.B: Because toxoplasmosis can mimic rejection, biopsy and further workup are needed rather than assuming identical untreatable presentations.
rationale_incorrect.C: Fever and graft dysfunction warrant diagnostic evaluation rather than unilateral immunosuppression cessation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Urinary amylase is a pancreas graft monitoring test, not the primary diagnostic approach for heart-lung rejection versus toxoplasmosis.

stem: A coordinator is teaching long-term self-care to a bladder-drained pancreas transplant recipient. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Dehydration and metabolic acidosis may remain lifelong complications for bladder-drained pancreas grafts.
The pancreas graft has higher thrombosis risk when intravascular volume is inadequate.
Adequate oral fluid intake is unimportant after pancreas transplantation.
Poor skin turgor may indicate dehydration requiring team notification.

explanation.rationale_correct: Bladder-drained pancreas recipients may have lifelong dehydration and metabolic acidosis risk; the low-flow graft is thrombosis-prone with hypovolemia; dehydration signs such as poor skin turgor should be reported; adequate oral fluids are emphasized to minimize hypotension and graft risk.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—poor skin turgor is a dehydration indicator requiring reporting.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statements I and II are also true; statement III is false because oral fluid intake is important.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false; adequate oral fluid intake is part of long-term pancreas graft care.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 15, Pancreas Transplantation → fluid management and patient education
primary_anchor.quote_hint: dehydration and metabolic acidosis will remain potential posttransplant complications for the life of the pancreas graft … low blood flow … graft thrombosis … Poor skin turgor … adequate oral fluid intake

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 15 → fluid management and H. Patient/caregiver education (lifelong dehydration/acidosis risk, thrombosis with hypovolemia, dehydration signs, oral fluid intake); PDF p. 838 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

stem: A pediatric intestinal transplant recipient refuses most oral intake despite medical clearance to eat. Which post-transplant coordination priority aligns with standard references?

options.text: Coordinate feeding support addressing oral aversion common in pediatric intestinal recipients
Ignore feeding refusal because oral intake is never part of intestinal transplant recovery
Discharge immediately without any feeding or nutrition resources
Permanently stop all immunosuppression because of poor oral intake

explanation.rationale_correct: Oral aversion is common before and after intestine transplantation, particularly in pediatric recipients, and requires coordinated feeding support addressing gag reflex, taste changes, and related behavioral factors.

rationale_incorrect.B: Oral intake and feeding progression are central to intestinal transplant recovery rather than being irrelevant.
rationale_incorrect.C: Nutrition and feeding support are ongoing coordination needs rather than omitted at discharge.
rationale_incorrect.D: Feeding difficulties are managed with multidisciplinary support rather than unilateral immunosuppression cessation.
